newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-TEAM CHAMPIONS NOW LOOK FOR INDIVIDUAL SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-TEAM CHAMPIONS NOW LOOK FOR INDIVIDUAL SUCCESS.

text.p: After helping China to retain the Sudirman Cup with a 5-0 win over South Korea in the final, world number one Dong Jiong said he had achieved his most important target at the world badminton championships.

But now the All-England champion has his sights firmly set on becoming the first Chinese man since Zhao Jianhua, in Copenhagen in 1991, to lift the men's singles title in the individual championships which start on Tuesday.

Dong is the number one seed but will face a stiff challenge from Olympic champion Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen of Denmark, who showed a welcome return to form with victory over the defending world champion Heryanto Arbi of Indonesia in the team event.
Having realised his Olympic dream in Atlanta, the Dane admits his form tailed off.
"But the win over Arbi was very important," he said. "Mentally, I now feel I am back to 100 per cent."
In the women's singles, All-England champion and world number one Ye Zhaoying is the top seed. But a shock defeat by Susi Susanti of Indonesia in the team event will have dented her confidence.
Susanti, who recently married former Olympic champion Allan Budi Kusuma, is seeded only fifth but she will be the popular favourite in Glasgow.
The 26-year-old Susanti has been threatening to retire for some time and a repeat of her 1993 victory in Birmingham would be the perfect end to her world championship career.
Susanti is due to meet number two seed Gong Zhichao of China in the quarter-finals.

Denmark's Camilla Martin is the leading European hope but the number four seed will have to overcome two Chinese players, the 1995 beaten finalist Han Jingna and Zhang Ning, if she is to reach the final.
